citeAs: Lu, P., Bansal, H., Xia, T., Liu, J., Li, C., Hajishirzi, H., Cheng, H., Chang, K.-W., Galley, M., & Gao, J. (2024). MATHVISTA: EVALUATING MATHEMATICAL REASONING OF FOUNDATION MODELS IN VISUAL CONTEXTS. ICLR 2024.
creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao (UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research)
description: MATHVISTA is a consolidated mathematical reasoning benchmark in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets, designed to evaluate the mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visually intensive scenarios.
name: MATHVISTA
publisher: UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research
rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields (for new datasets) and human annotators with a high school diploma or higher (for VQA filtering).
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: High inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2%. Among the newly collected 736 questions, only 6 exhibited disagreements. Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775, indicating a substantial level of consistency among the annotators.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) and a custom GUI annotation tool.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Initially, each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers. Discrepancies were resolved through discussion among the entire review team, ensuring a consensus was reached on each example.
rai:dataCollection: Incorporates 28 existing multimodal datasets (limited to up to 400 examples each) and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA). For existing VQA datasets, heuristic rules automatically selected examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning, followed by manual labeling by expert annotators.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: 28 existing multimodal datasets, puzzle test figures on online learning platforms, functional plots, and academic illustrations (tables, figures, charts) from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
rai:dataLimitations: Dataset coverage may have gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. Annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples having annotations, which lack a unified format and structure.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Heuristic rules to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning from a large pool of candidates. Examples with numeric answers or those containing quantity words in the questions were selected.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The answer labels for the test set will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination, and an online evaluation platform will be maintained. The authors are committed to maintaining the datasets, refining potential data noise in response to community feedback, and evolving the leaderboard.
rai:dataUseCases: Facilitate the development of mathematical reasoning systems in visually intensive scenarios, and evaluate the research progress of LLMs and LMMs in solving rigorous reasoning tasks.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Heuristic rules were used to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning from a large pool of candidates.
